cases.what_created: Telephone invented and patented by Alexander Graham Bell.
Bell's key patents expired and thousands of independent local telephone companies started.
cases.source: Brooks, J., Telephone: The First Hundred Years (Harper & Row, 1976); exact year of the surge is approximate.

cases.what_created: Mann-Elkins Act put interstate telephone service under the Interstate Commerce Commission.
Kingsbury Commitment: AT&T agreed to let independents connect to its network after antitrust pressure.
cases.source: Brooks, J., Telephone: The First Hundred Years (Harper & Row, 1976).

cases.what_created: Communications Act of 1934 created the Federal Communications Commission.
Break-up of AT&T into regional companies under a court-approved settlement.
cases.source: United States v. AT&T, Modified Final Judgment (D.D.C. 1982, effective 1984).

cases.what_created: Telecommunications Act of 1996 opened local phone markets to competition.
Spoofed robocalls became the top consumer complaint to regulators.
cases.source: FCC Consumer Complaint Data Center; the FCC has listed unwanted calls as its top consumer complaint category. Year is approximate.

cases.what_created: TRACED Act required carriers to authenticate caller ID.
STIR/SHAKEN call-authentication technology required on major carrier networks.
cases.source: FCC, 'Combating Spoofed Robocalls with Caller ID Authentication'; June 30, 2021 deadline for large providers.
